skill.title: Classify a function as injective, surjective, bijective
needs: Recognise a function and its domain/codomain/range

note: Each problem gives a function with its domain and codomain (vary them: a linear map R→R, a quadratic on a restricted domain, a map between small finite sets or N→N) and asks the student to decide whether it is injective, surjective and bijective, with a reason for each. The worked solution tests BOTH injectivity (equal outputs force equal inputs, or a counterexample) AND surjectivity (solve f(x) = y for a general y in the codomain, or find a value never reached), then classifies. finalSym: 1 if bijective, 0 if not; answerSym computes that from the givens (e.g. a test case such as the number of preimages). The references show the exam style only; they cover just part of the skill.

steps.title: Assume two inputs give the same output

lines.text: $f$ is injective if $f(a) = f(b)$ forces $a = b$.

steps.title: Solve for a

lines.text: Different inputs always give different outputs, so $f$ is injective.

references.final: f(a) = f(b) \Rightarrow a = b \text{, so } f \text{ is injective}

skill.title: Test whether a point is on a line; find intercepts

note: Each problem gives one line (vary the form: ax + by + c = 0, y = mx + c, fractions or a negative slope) and asks the student to find where it cuts the x-axis and the y-axis, AND to test whether a given point is on the line. The worked solution does both: set y = 0 and x = 0 for the intercepts, then substitute the point and compare. One problem should have the point on the line, one off it. finalSym: the two intercepts as a list of points, e.g. [(4, 0), (0, -6)]; answerSym solves for them from the line. The references show the exam style only; they cover just part of the skill.

steps.title: Substitute x = -2 and y = -5 into x - y - 3

lines.text: The left side equals $0$, so $T$ is on $k$.

steps.title: Substitute x = -2 and y = 1 into 4x + 3y + 5
Compare both sides of the equation

lines.text: The left side equals $0$, which is the right side, so $P$ is on $k$.

steps.title: Substitute x = -1 and y = 5 into 3x - 2y + 7
Compare with 0

lines.text: The left side equals $-6$, not $0$, so the point is not on $l$.

skill.title: Compare data sets with back-to-back stem-and-leaf plots
needs: Draw bar, pie, line plot, histogram and stem-and-leaf
Find quartiles and the interquartile range

note: Each problem gives two small data sets (12 to 16 values each, real contexts: reaction times, heights, scores) and asks the student to draw a back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot AND compare the two sets using the median and the range. The worked solution orders each set, describes the plot (stems in the middle, leaves outward, a key), finds each median and range, and writes a one-sentence comparison of centre and spread. finalSym: [median A, median B, range A, range B]; answerSym computes them from the data (e.g. with Rational for medians). The references show the exam style only; they cover just part of the skill.

steps.title: Put the stem for each value in its row

lines.text: The stem is the tens (and hundreds) part. The leaf is the units digit.
Sort the leaves in each row so they increase moving away from the stem.

steps.title: Fill in the before-exercise leaves (left side)

lines.text: $70, 76, 77$ go in row 7 as leaves $0, 6, 7$.
$83, 88, 89$ go in row 8 as leaves $3, 8, 9$.

steps.title: Fill in the after-exercise leaves (right side)

lines.text: $102, 108$ in row 10 as leaves $2, 8$. $113, 118$ in row 11 as leaves $3, 8$.

steps.title: Split each mark into a stem and a leaf

lines.text: The stem is the tens digit and the leaf is the units digit. The key $3 | 5 = 35$ marks means stem 3 and leaf 5 give 35.

steps.title: List the Class A leaves for each stem

lines.text: Stem 2: 23, 27, 29 so leaves 3, 7, 9.
Stem 4: 42, 44 so leaves 2, 4.

steps.title: List the Class B leaves for each stem

lines.text: Stem 2: 25, 28 so leaves 5, 8.

steps.title: Draw the plot with leaves in order outwards

lines.text: Put Class A leaves on the left of the stem and Class B leaves on the right, smallest next to the stem.
Check: each side has 10 leaves, one for each student.

steps.title: Put the Week 2 values in order
Group the values by stem
Write the leaves on the left of the stem

lines.text: Put the smallest leaf of each row next to the stem, so the leaves get bigger as they move left. Check that 2 + 8 + 4 + 1 + 1 = 16 leaves are shown.
